title: Wendell and the Horizon
premise: Orsen Eriksen, an insurance investigator sent to assess the failing colony of Wendell's Landing, discovers its records are being quietly falsified by a corporate consortium that abandoned the settlement years ago. The colony's children begin sharing a dream of a horizon that speaks, a signal from a derelict alien relay that holds the key to ending the interstellar war. When the consortium moves to erase the colony—and the evidence—Orsen must choose between filing his report and becoming its messenger. In the end, he broadcasts the truth at the cost of his own safe anonymity, and the colony's found family carries his message to a ceasefire that begins with the children's dream.
about_author: Ansel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who traded harbor offices for starships in his fiction. His work explores the paperwork of catastrophe and the quiet heroism of people who read the fine print.

chapters.title: The Fine Print of Falling Stars
chapters.summary: Orsen Eriksen arrives at Wendell's Landing to investigate a shuttle crash that shouldn't have been survivable, finding a colony of two hundred the ledgers claim was evacuated. Told from Orsen's POV, he notices the children watching him with unsettling recognition. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking at the edges as he realizes he's been sent not to assess the colony, but to close its file.

chapters.title: Children of the Shared Horizon
chapters.summary: Orsen interviews colonists and discovers every child under twelve dreams the same dream: a glowing horizon that whispers coordinates. POV shifts to Mara, a schoolteacher raising the orphans of the evacuation that never happened. Emotional beat: tenderness and dread entwine as Mara realizes the dreams began the night the last supply ship was turned away.

chapters.title: Actuarial Ghosts
chapters.summary: Orsen traces falsified death certificates and discovers the consortium declared Wendell's Landing a total loss years ago—everyone here is legally dead, which makes their land free for salvage. POV: Orsen, in the colony archive. Emotional beat: cold fury as he understands his report is the murder weapon, and the colonists know it.

chapters.title: What the Dream Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's oldest charge, a girl named Iva, draws the horizon dream in perfect detail—and it matches an ancient relay chart in the consortium's sealed records. POV: Iva, dreamlike and precise. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear when Iva reveals the dream has started including a man in an investigator's coat, standing at the edge.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Never Here
chapters.summary: Orsen's handler orders him to certify the colony as uninhabited within ten days. He uncovers that the relay the children dream of is a pre-war alien transmitter capable of broadcasting unjammable across the war front. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the vertigo of choosing a side—his invisible life versus two hundred dead-on-paper people.

chapters.title: A Family Assembled from Scraps
chapters.summary: The colonists, knowing Orsen's report dooms them, take him in anyway—shared meals, mended coats, a birthday celebrated a week late for his benefit. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: Orsen experiences found family for the first time and realizes he has already betrayed them by hesitating; duty and love pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Ten Days to Silence
chapters.summary: A consortium salvage fleet is dispatched; the children's dream intensifies, now showing the horizon burning. Orsen and Iva decode the coordinates: the relay will broadcast one message, once, to both warring fleets. POV: alternating Orsen and Iva. Emotional beat: rising panic and resolve as the deadline becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Weight of One Message
chapters.summary: The message requires a living mind to carry it into the relay—a human who has both dreamed the horizon and understood the ledgers. Only Orsen qualifies. The colonists vote to let him go, knowing the broadcast will expose the consortium and bring retaliation on Wendell's Landing. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the terrible cost of being seen.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Climax: as the salvage fleet burns the settlement's outskirts, Orsen reaches the relay and speaks the children's dream aloud—the coordinates of a shared origin that proves both warring factions descend from the same lost colony. The broadcast seizes every fleet channel at once. POV: Orsen, dissolving into the signal. Emotional beat: sacrifice, awe, and the horizon finally opening.

chapters.title: After the Signal, the Morning
chapters.summary: Ceasefire fleets arrive not as conquerors but as witnesses; the consortium's falsified ledgers become evidence of war crimes. Mara and the children rebuild, and in the first dreamless night in a year, Iva dreams only of Orsen, standing at a horizon that is finally just a horizon. POV: Iva, closing. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance—memory, love, and a family that endures.
